text:
maya: Quick sync — we need a crisp heuristic for tier entitlements when customers mix reserved capacity + hosted API. Sales is asking for explicit rules.

dan: tl;dr: if reserved_commit >= 70% of historical peak -> treat as Dedicated quota else as Hosted with burst credits.

sarah: Can we avoid hard percentages? customers will push back. Maybe two signals: commit_ratio and sustained_peak_days.

kevin: Agree with Sarah. Example: commit_ratio = commit / 90th_percentile_peak; sustained_peak_days = days over 80% of commit in last 30d.

emily: +1. Also need a fallback path for contracts: if legal signs a clause saying "dedicated-like SLA" we should map to Dedicated regardless of metrics.

maya: Good point. Sales will always try to encode. We need a canonical ordering: 1) explicit contract carveouts, 2) admin flag (support request), 3) metrics heuristic, 4) default to Hosted.

alex: For rollout, propose making the heuristic advisory in Console (show recommended mapping) for 2 weeks, then auto-enforce with opt-out. That gives us telemetry.

dan: How do we compute cost impact? We should simulate on last 90 days of meter data and show projected delta.

pricing-bot: FYI: projected unit-cost delta function available as /pricing/simulate?period=90d&granularity=daily (returns CSV).

kevin: Nice. Also edge-case: multi-model workloads where some models are only in Hosted catalog. In that case mapping commit -> Dedicated is invalid unless model pinning to hosted-compatible variant exists. We need an incompatibility flag in the heuristic.

maya: Right. Add rule: if any route references model tagged "hosted-only" -> mark as "incompatible with Dedicated" and surface to AE.

emily: For launch criteria: 1) docs and Console UX showing the mapping, 2) simulation job for existing customers, 3) two customer pilots (sales + 1) and 4) metric: <1% auto-mapped false positives after 30 days.

alex: Ops ask: what about billing adjustments? If we remap a customer from Hosted -> Dedicated mid-billing-cycle should we prorate? Sales prefers prorate credits vs. invoices. Need decision.

maya: Policy: for first 90 days of the feature, do not change billing retroactively; instead, create an "onboarding credit" if mapping error discovered. Post-90d we can consider prorate. Document and sync with finance.

dan: Implementation sketch (config snippet):
```yaml
entitlement_heuristic:
  precedence:
    - contract_carveout
    - admin_override
    - metrics_rule
    - default_hosted
  metrics_rule:
    commit_ratio_threshold: 0.7
    sustained_peak_days_threshold: 10
    incompatibility_tags: ["hosted-only"]
```

sarah: That looks fine. For customer-facing language keep it non-technical: "We recommend mapping X to Dedicated because their committed capacity covers regular peaks."

kevin: One operational note: we must log the decision with the key signals for audit (contract id, commit_ratio, peak_days, any admin override). Security wants this stored for 365 days.

maya: Ok. Action items: @dan run simulation on top 200 customers by spend by EOD Fri, @alex draft Console copy + telemetry UI, @emily work with sales to pick 2 pilots. I'll draft the policy for finance and legal.

alex: I'll also add a small modal action in Console: "Review recommended mapping" with links to the simulation CSV and a one-click request for admin override.

emily: Picking pilots: suggest Acorn and Slate.io — both have mixed usage. I'll reach out.

pricing-bot: Note: simulation job queued (id: sim-20260322-42). ETA 4h.

maya: Great. We'll reconvene Mon for readout. :thumbsup:
